races.name: Connolly's Red Mills Open Hunters' Chase

runners_data.name: Franigane
runners_data.note: Front runner returning after 364 days off with blinkers fitted, but his style suits small fields where he won't face early pressure

runners_data.name: On Lovers Walk
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in excellent recent form with tongue tie applied and trainer Kelly Morgan showing perfect recent record

runners_data.name: Great Valley
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with clear class advantage (OR 127) and solid recent form, though amateur jockey Mr Guy Sankey adds slight question mark

races.paceDynamic: Franigane will lead from the start with his confirmed front-running style, setting what should be a manageable pace given the small field and lack of other genuine pace horses. On Lovers Walk and Great Valley will both track prominently behind, creating a compact group throughout. With no genuine hold-up horses and limited early pressure on Franigane, this sets up as a sustained gallop that will favour the most talented horse who can quicken from a prominent position. This race shape strongly favours the prominent runners who can travel well and have a decisive turn of foot.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Great Valley Dominates Class
scenarios.trigger: If Great Valley travels smoothly in second behind Franigane's moderate pace
scenarios.body: His superior class (OR 127) and good recent form will tell as he quickens decisively from the last fence. The sustained gallop will suit his prominent style perfectly against these inferior rivals.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: On Lovers Walk Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes stronger than expected or Great Valley doesn't handle the track
scenarios.body: On Lovers Walk's excellent recent record (1/24f last time) and trainer Kelly Morgan's 100% strike rate in last 14 days gives her the edge. Her prominent style thrives when the pace is honest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Franigane Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Franigane gets loose on the lead and the others fail to close
scenarios.body: Despite his 364-day layoff, his front-running style could steal this if he gets an uncontested lead and finds his old form. The small field helps him avoid interference and pressure.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Shock
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is crawling and it becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The lack of genuine pace could create a messy finish where any of the three could prevail based on jumping and position at the last. Form lines become less reliable in a slowly-run race.

watchPoints.text: Great Valley's jumping under pressure - amateur rider Mr Guy Sankey may struggle if the race becomes tactical
Franigane's fitness after 364 days off - any signs of rustiness early could end his chances quickly
On Lovers Walk's ability to quicken - needs to prove she can match Great Valley's superior class rating
Early pace development - if Franigane gets loose on the lead the complexion changes completely
Jumping at the last fence - in a small field finish, one mistake could be decisive for any of the three

races.name: Pertemps Network Intermediate Point-To-Point Hunters' Chase

runners_data.name: Ultimate Survivor
runners_data.note: Lightly raced unknown quantity with no clear running style - major tactical wildcard that could disrupt expected pace scenario

runners_data.name: Mister Splash
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with solid recent form who needs others to go fast early but has proven finishing kick over similar trips

runners_data.name: Fame And Concrete
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with good course record who should sit handy to The Dancing Tree and has tactical speed to respond

runners_data.name: Practice Run
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from long break who needs strong pace to aim at but has solid staying form when fit

runners_data.name: The Dancing Tree
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner in excellent form who will want to make all and has tactical advantage of controlling tempo

runners_data.name: Tellmesomethingood
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been running consistently but may struggle to make up ground if pace is too steady early

races.paceDynamic: The Dancing Tree will dictate terms from the front with Fame And Concrete sitting prominently, creating a steady but undemanding gallop in the early stages. With three hold-up horses (Mister Splash, Practice Run, Tellmesomethingood) and Ultimate Survivor's unknown style, there's limited early pressure on the leaders. The pace will build gradually through the middle section before accelerating from three out. This sustainable tempo strongly favours prominent racers and front runners who can control the race, while hold-up horses face the challenge of making up ground against horses who've had an easy lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If The Dancing Tree and Fame And Concrete dominate the early pace without pressure
scenarios.body: The leaders dictate comfortable fractions and have energy reserves for the finish. Hold-up horses struggle to peg back the advantage against horses who've had an armchair ride.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Challenge Success
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses get strong runs from the back and the pace quickens late
scenarios.body: Mister Splash and Practice Run benefit from their patient tactics as the early leaders tire. The combination of class and fresh legs tells in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Ultimate Survivor Impact
scenarios.trigger: If Ultimate Survivor shows early speed and joins the pace battle
scenarios.body: The unknown quantity changes the complexion by creating genuine early pressure. This forces a stronger gallop that could suit a late finisher or compromise the front runners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If all runners converge turning for home in a slowly-run affair
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where positioning and momentum matter most. Any horse with tactical speed and good jumping rhythm can capitalise on the bunched field.

watchPoints.text: Ultimate Survivor's early positioning will reveal if this becomes a genuine pace battle or allows The Dancing Tree an easy lead
The Dancing Tree's jumping rhythm early on - any mistake could hand initiative to Fame And Concrete or invite pressure
How quickly Mister Splash and Practice Run get into contention turning for home after their patient early tactics
Fame And Concrete's willingness to press The Dancing Tree rather than sitting in behind and compromising hold-up horses
Tellmesomethingood's position at halfway - needs to be closer than usual given likely steady early gallop

races.name: GB Pointing Open Hunters' Chase

runners_data.name: What A Glance
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner facing a likely tactical pace that may not provide enough tempo for his late surge, plus the 49-day break adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Alaphilippe
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with uncontested lead likely, returning after 364 days but trainer cheekpieces suggest connections expect improvement.

runners_data.name: Laurel Girl
runners_data.note: Unraced for 1353 days making her impossible to assess despite her style being unknown, represents a complete wildcard.

runners_data.name: Mister Coffey
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner from powerful Henderson yard but recent form suggests decline, needs tactical race and return to better efforts.

runners_data.name: High Game Royal
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in excellent recent form with consistent placed efforts, perfectly positioned to track steady early pace.

races.paceDynamic: Alaphilippe will lead from the start with no genuine pace pressure in this small field of five. High Game Royal may track in second, but with What A Glance and Mister Coffey both preferring to come from behind, the early gallop will be sedate. The lack of sustained pace pressure through the middle stages will create a race where the leaders can conserve energy for a sprint finish. This tactical setup strongly favours the front-running and prominent runners who can control the tempo and have first run when the race develops.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alaphilippe Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Alaphilippe dictates an uncontested lead through halfway
scenarios.body: The 12-year-old can nurse his advantage and use his 364-day freshness break positively, kicking clear when the hold-up horses are still organizing behind. High Game Royal's prominent style puts him perfectly placed to capitalize if the leader falters.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: High Game Royal Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If High Game Royal tracks the steady pace and produces his customary strong finish
scenarios.body: The 9-year-old's recent good form and consistent placed efforts suit this tactical scenario perfectly. His prominent running style allows him to strike at the optimal moment when hold-up horses need more time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: What A Glance Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely slow and the hold-up horses get ideal racing room
scenarios.body: The 11-year-old's hold-up style could exploit a dawdling tempo, but needs everything to fall right including the 49-day break working in his favor. This scenario requires multiple pace collapses up front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Mister Coffey Henderson Magic
scenarios.trigger: If Nicky Henderson's charge finds significant improvement from his recent disappointing runs
scenarios.body: The 11-year-old would need both a tactical race to suit hold-up runners and a return to his better form. His trainer's 6/21 recent record provides some hope but form suggests he's vulnerable.

watchPoints.text: Laurel Girl's fitness after 1353 days off - if she shows early pace or travels strongly, it completely changes all tactical assumptions.
Alaphilippe's stamina reserves after 364 days off - watch for signs of fatigue in the final half-mile despite controlling the tempo.
What A Glance and Mister Coffey getting outpaced if High Game Royal quickens approaching the second-last fence.
High Game Royal's jumping rhythm tracking Alaphilippe - any early mistakes will compromise his tactical position.
The overall pace through halfway - if genuinely slow it opens the door for hold-up runners despite the small field dynamics.

races.name: Jonathan Neesom Memorial Open Hunters' Chase

runners_data.name: Crawter
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong recent Plumpton third, benefits from regular racing and good going preference but needs to prove stamina over this extended trip.

runners_data.name: Imperial Esprit
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner returning after 336-day absence, relies on class and course experience but fitness must be taken on trust given lengthy layoff.

runners_data.name: Kilfilum Woods
runners_data.note: Consistent performer with good going record, benefits from recent Exeter win but question marks over ability to quicken in small field tactical affair.

runners_data.name: Corporal Jackjones
runners_data.note: Strong recent form with back-to-back wins, shortest absence of 53 days gives fitness edge but must prove effectiveness when not dominating from the front.

races.paceDynamic: Imperial Esprit emerges as the sole confirmed pace-setter in this small field, with his consistent front-running style likely to dictate terms from the outset. All four runners show prominent tendencies, but Imperial Esprit's natural lead preference means he'll likely face minimal early pressure, allowing him to control the gallop over this extended trip. Crawter and Corporal Jackjones possess the tactical speed to track closely, while Kilfilum Woods may settle slightly further back given his more patient recent campaigns. This sustainable pace scenario heavily favours horses with the tactical pace to respond when Imperial Esprit kicks, making prominent runners with finishing pace the profile to follow.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Imperial Esprit Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Imperial Esprit gets an uncontested lead and maintains rhythm throughout
scenarios.body: His 12-year-old experience allows him to judge the pace perfectly, kicking clear at the optimal moment when others struggle to respond. The combination of tactical advantage and recent consistency proves decisive over this stamina-testing distance.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Pace Injection
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely searching with multiple horses tracking Imperial Esprit closely
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop sets up perfectly for horses with proven finishing kicks, as Imperial Esprit's long absence begins to tell in the final half-mile. Fresh legs and recent racecourse experience become the determining factors.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If Crawter or Corporal Jackjones challenge Imperial Esprit earlier than expected in the home straight
scenarios.body: The pace becomes genuinely competitive from three out, creating opportunities for any horse still travelling smoothly to capitalise on the leaders' efforts. Superior fitness levels and tactical positioning prove crucial.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Imperial Esprit fails to fire after his lengthy absence and the pace becomes crawling
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the home turn, suiting horses with instant acceleration rather than sustained galloping ability. Recent race fitness and sharp speed become premium assets in a tactical finish.

watchPoints.text: Imperial Esprit's jumping rhythm early on - any hesitancy suggests his lengthy absence is telling and undermines his tactical advantage.
Crawter's position tracking Imperial Esprit - if he's unable to sit close, his finishing kick becomes compromised over this stamina-sapping distance.
Corporal Jackjones settling pattern - recent front-running wins may have made him keen, and fighting for his head would compromise his finishing effort.
Kilfilum Woods travelling smoothly turning for home - his patient style needs others to set strong gallop to be effective.
The pace through halfway - if genuinely steady, it transforms into sprint finish favouring horses with instant acceleration over sustained galloping ability.

races.paceDynamic: Loud And Proud is the only confirmed leader and should get an easy time on the front with Hollywood Harmon and All Loved Up the only prominent runners to provide any early company. The pace will be steady rather than strong given the lack of early pressure, allowing the front section to travel comfortably through the middle stages. With five hold-up horses including top-rated For Rita and improving Police Academy, this becomes a tactical affair where the leaders can dictate. This race shape clearly favours front runners and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will engulf the large hold-up contingent.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leaders Control Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Loud And Proud gets uncontested lead and Hollywood Harmon tracks comfortably
scenarios.body: The pace stays steady enough for the front pair to have energy for the finish while hold-up horses struggle to make up ground from poor positions. Traffic and positioning issues compound problems for the back markers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong or leaders tire dramatically
scenarios.body: Police Academy or For Rita benefits from a strong gallop that sets up their preferred come-from-behind style perfectly. The class edge of these hold-up performers tells when others have emptied their tanks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Hollywood Harmon positions perfectly behind Loud And Proud and times run ideally
scenarios.body: The prominent runner avoids early pace pressure but stays close enough to strike when it matters most. Superior positioning gives crucial advantage over both leaders and hold-up horses stuck behind.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Loud And Proud stops quickly and early pace becomes crawling slow
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where any horse can win regardless of early position. Form and class become less relevant than who gets the clearest run when the race ignites late.

watchPoints.text: Loud And Proud could have fitness issues after 153-day layoff when pace quickens in straight

races.paceDynamic: Myth Buster will lead from the start with no other confirmed front-runners in this small field. The veteran 13-year-old should dictate a steady gallop over the marathon 4m1f trip, with Jeffery's Cross, My Gift To You and Slipway tracking in a compact group behind. Peaches And Cream will drop out last under hold-up tactics. This sustainable pace setup strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and kick from the final half-mile, making front-running difficult to sustain and hold-up tactics risky over such a staying trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Myth Buster sets reasonable fractions and the prominent horses travel well
scenarios.body: The race becomes a staying test where the classier prominent racers can time their challenge perfectly from close range. Jeffery's Cross or Slipway benefit most from tracking the leader before asserting superior stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sustained Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Myth Buster gets soft sectionals and maintains strong jumping rhythm throughout
scenarios.body: The veteran leader capitalises on his early advantage and proven stamina to repel late challenges. His 97 days off could work positively for freshness over this extreme distance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Hold-Up Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes overly conservative and bunches the field
scenarios.body: Peaches And Cream gets the perfect setup to unleash her finishing kick from the rear. The compact field and steady gallop allows her hold-up style to be devastating late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Myth Buster goes too fast early or makes jumping errors under pressure

My Gift To You's fitness levels after 189 days away - could find the sustained gallop too much if ring-rusty
Slipway's position tracking - needs to be handy turning for home to utilise his class advantage
Peaches And Cream's ability to close the gap if the pace quickens approaching the final circuit

runners_data.name: Hystery Bere
runners_data.note: Hold-up style runner returning after 159 days with claiming jockey, making this a stepping stone rather than winning target

runners_data.name: Fan De Blues
runners_data.note: Another hold-up horse who needs the pace to collapse, with 22 days since last run keeping him fresh

runners_data.name: Empire De Maulde

runners_data.name: Arthur's Sixpence
runners_data.note: Front-runner who gets ideal tactical scenario but faces significant class deficit, with 42 days since last run

races.paceDynamic: Arthur's Sixpence will dictate from the front with no other confirmed pace angles, allowing him to set a comfortable rhythm over this 2m4f trip. The three hold-up horses (Hystery Bere, Fan De Blues, Empire De Maulde) will settle behind while Unexpected Party tracks in a prominent position. With no pace pressure on the leader, this creates a tactical race where Arthur's Sixpence can control the tempo and potentially steal a march, though it also sets up perfectly for the superior-rated Unexpected Party to time a challenge from a tracking position. This pace scenario clearly favours prominent runners who can position close enough to the uncontested leader while having the class edge to strike.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Arthur's Sixpence gets an easy lead and maintains momentum turning for home
scenarios.body: The 12-year-old can dictate his own fractions without pressure and use his front-running style to maximum advantage. His three wins from 15 runs on good going shows he can handle these conditions when getting the right race shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class Tells From Tracking
scenarios.trigger: If Unexpected Party gets the perfect trip tracking Arthur's Sixpence and produces her superior turn of foot
scenarios.body: The OR 145-rated mare has the tactical speed to sit prominent and the class edge over this field when the race develops. Her recent course form (2P114) shows she's in good heart for Dan Skelton.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly pedestrian and allows one of the back markers to unleash a decisive late run
scenarios.body: Empire De Maulde's dual experience on good going and 2W7P record from 15 runs gives him the profile to capitalise if the race falls apart. His hold-up style needs the tempo to collapse completely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddle Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Arthur's Sixpence goes too slow early then quickens, catching the hold-up horses napping
scenarios.body: Fan De Blues could benefit from a messy tactical affair where his hold-up style gets the right gaps at the right time. His trainer Miss Nikki Henton sends out few runners so this represents a targeted opportunity.

watchPoints.text: Arthur's Sixpence must be watched for early pace - if he goes off too hard he'll empty out, if too slow he hands initiative to Unexpected Party
Unexpected Party's jumping must be monitored closely as any mistake will hand Arthur's Sixpence crucial momentum in a small field
The three amateur jockeys (Neal, Williams, O'Connor) on the hold-up horses need to position perfectly as there will be limited opportunities in a slowly-run race
Empire De Maulde showed promise on good going but 42 days off makes his current wellbeing crucial to assess in the preliminaries
Fan De Blues needs to be watched for market confidence given trainer Miss Nikki Henton's low strike rate but targeted approach
